questions.question: On most roads, signal at least ____ before you turn.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes on most roads. On highways, signal at least 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: Your body processes approximately:
questions.explanation: The average person's body processes one alcoholic drink per hour. How impaired someone becomes depends on many factors: the amount consumed, how fast they drink, body weight, food intake, and general health.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with opposite traffic, you should:

options.text: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the passed vehicle.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the passed vehicle.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right side once there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming hazards. This sign warns you that bicycles may cross here.

questions.question: On a highway, signal at least ____ before you turn.
questions.explanation: On the highway, signal at least 500 feet before turning or changing lanes.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, slow down:

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
When you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane well before your exit. Only slow down after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: Driving faster:

options.text: Makes it easier to see cross traffic.
Does not affect your field of vision.

questions.explanation: As your speed increases, your field of vision gets smaller. You must stay extra alert for hazards as you drive faster.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle that just parked on the roadside, you should:

options.text: Expect the driver to open the door as you pass.
Assume the driver will wait until you pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the driver to open the door as you pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked vehicle, be ready for the driver to open the door. Drive carefully near parked cars.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: What is reasonable and safe for conditions.
A speed safe for existing conditions.

questions.explanation: Drive at a safe, reasonable speed for the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road condition, and light. Always follow posted speed limits.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to get other drivers to let you through.
Drive around the back of a car that blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you turn. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway angles toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: You are approaching a construction area.
You will need to turn left soon.

questions.explanation: A solid line on the edge of the road marks the boundary between the travel lane and shoulder. When the edge line angles toward the center of the road, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left and you both reach an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when you enter a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on the intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs tell you to stop and yield the right-of-way at an intersection. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: When you turn right on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You can turn right or left at a steady green light unless a sign says otherwise. When turning, you must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown.
A divided highway starts. Slow down to the safe speed shown.
Merge ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown.
The road winds ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves to the right ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown, which in this case is 35 mph.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: You have done all you need to do.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit an unattended parked car, stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot, leave a written note with your name, address, and details about the accident.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection. The light is green but there is heavy oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Go because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with oncoming traffic, wait for that traffic to pass before you turn. You can enter the intersection to prepare if the light is green and no other car is turning left ahead of you.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and go when it is safe.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "caution." Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign tells you to slow down and let other traffic in the intersection or on the road you are entering go first.

questions.question: You may not park within ____ of a fire hydrant.
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. Park in legal spots where drivers can clearly see your vehicle from both directions.

questions.question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and you can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: You may cross solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass traffic moving the same direction.

questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You can only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: When should you use hand-over-hand steering?

options.text: When backing up or using turn signals, radio, or wipers

questions.explanation: Use hand-over-hand steering when turning slowly, like at an intersection or when parking. Put your left hand between 8 and 9 o'clock and your right hand between 3 and 4 o'clock on the wheel.

questions.question: When you see reduced visibility, you should first:
questions.explanation: Slowing down should be your first action when visibility is poor and road conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and you can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A solid line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: You reach an intersection with a flashing red light. You must:

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. Then you can go when the path is clear.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing.
Run in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street without an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be careful around children. They may not understand danger and could run in front of your car without looking.

questions.question: Under normal weather and traffic, keep a minimum following distance of:
questions.explanation: More space between your car and others gives you more time to react. Keep at least four seconds of distance in normal conditions. Increase this distance in bad weather or heavy traffic.
